recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If OO wants a literal cancelled code or different wording in current RequestStatus, raise that as a new current-build terminology issue rather than reopening the retired DiagnosticOrder-specific work.
issue_request: FHIR-5854 was a Published/Persuasive OO change request from DSTU1 asking to add Draft and Cancelled concepts to the DiagnosticOrder.status value set, with Draft meaning preliminary before being sent and Cancelled meaning withdrawn.
initial_application: Git-svn commit cd3cbf8d9dd13675993f7872d512d8c72541c4c5 explicitly included #5854 DiagnosticOrder and added draft/cancelled to the DiagnosticOrder status worksheet and short labels.
additional_context: FHIR-10295 later renamed DiagnosticOrder to DiagnosticRequest/request semantics, and current source/fhir.ini lists DiagnosticOrder under removed resources as subsumed into ServiceRequest. ServiceRequest is active and required-binds ServiceRequest.status to ValueSet/request-status, whose CodeSystem includes draft and the current withdrawal/termination concept revoked.
reconciliation: No source change was made because editing removed DiagnosticOrder source would not affect the current build, and changing current normative request-status terminology from revoked to cancelled would be a broader new request-pattern terminology decision rather than residual FHIR-5854 application.

related_jiras.note: Published/Persuasive rename of Order resources to Request resources; explains why DiagnosticOrder is no longer an active current artifact and why the current successor is ServiceRequest/request-pattern status.
